Variance components and fitted term variances for GAMs

Source: R/gamm4-methods.R, R/scam-methods.R, R/variance-components.R
variance_comp.Rd

Extract variance components for smooth penalties and random effects, or calculate the variances and covariances of fitted term contributions.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'gamm4'
variance_comp(
  object,
  rescale = TRUE,
  coverage = 0.95,
  interval_method = c("profile", "none"),
  type = c("penalty", "terms"),
  n_draws = 1000L,
  seed = NULL,
  unconditional = FALSE,
  include_total = TRUE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'scam'
variance_comp(
  object,
  rescale = TRUE,
  coverage = 0.95,
  type = c("penalty", "terms"),
  n_draws = 1000L,
  seed = NULL,
  unconditional = FALSE,
  include_total = TRUE,
  ...
)

variance_comp(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gam'
variance_comp(
  object,
  rescale = TRUE,
  coverage = 0.95,
  type = c("penalty", "terms"),
  n_draws = 1000L,
  seed = NULL,
  unconditional = FALSE,
  include_total = TRUE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'gamm'
variance_comp(
  object,
  rescale = TRUE,
  coverage = 0.95,
  type = c("penalty", "terms"),
  n_draws = 1000L,
  seed = NULL,
  unconditional = FALSE,
  include_total = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

a model fitted by mgcv::gam(), mgcv::bam(), mgcv::gamm(), or gamm4::gamm4(). See gamm4_support for mixed-model variance components.

rescale

logical; for numerical stability reasons the penalty matrices of smooths are rescaled before fitting. If rescale = TRUE, this rescaling is undone, resulting in variance components that are on their original scale. This is needed if comparing with other mixed model software, such as lmer().

coverage

numeric; a value between 0 and 1 indicating the (approximate) coverage of the confidence interval that is returned.

interval_method

character; for gamm4() fits, "profile" computes likelihood profile intervals and "none" returns estimates only.

type

character; "penalty" (the default) returns variance parameters associated with penalties and random effects. "terms" returns sample variances of fitted term contributions and their covariance matrix.

n_draws

integer; number of joint posterior coefficient draws for type = "terms". Defaults to 1000. Use zero for point estimates only; otherwise at least two draws are required. Ignored for type = "penalty".

seed

optional random seed for term intervals. Supplying a seed preserves the caller's random-number state.

unconditional

logical; include the available correction for smoothing-parameter uncertainty in term intervals. Defaults to FALSE. If the corrected covariance is unavailable, a warning is issued and the uncorrected covariance is used. SCAM fits require FALSE.

include_total

logical; include total rows for type = "terms"? Defaults to TRUE. Ignored for type = "penalty".

...

arguments passed to other methods. For gamm4() fits, additional arguments are passed to stats::profile(), for example maxpts. With type = "terms", no additional arguments are accepted.

Value

A tibble of class variance_comp, with .component, .variance, .std_dev, .lower_ci and .upper_ci. Both confidence limits are on the standard deviation scale. For type = "terms", obtain the named covariance matrix with attr(result, "covariance") and posterior variance draws with attr(result, "variance_draws") when intervals were computed. Term results also include proportion estimates and their interval columns; attr(result, "proportion_draws") contains the paired posterior proportions.

Details

For SCAM fits with type = "penalty", .variance is the fitted response scale divided by the smoothing parameter, optionally undoing penalty rescaling. This ratio describes the Gaussian penalty on unrestricted fitting parameters; it is not a Gaussian variance for the transformed smooth coefficients. SCAM's GCV and UBRE fits do not supply the likelihood-based smoothing-parameter covariance needed for confidence limits, so both limit columns are NA.

With type = "penalty", models fitted by mgcv::gam() and mgcv::bam() have one row per penalty, including penalties supplied through paraPen. Fixed smoothing parameters are included, and terms sharing a smoothing parameter each have their own rows. A smooth with several penalties has several rows. Unpenalized parametric terms have no variance parameter and are omitted.

The variance component is the fitted scale parameter divided by the smoothing parameter. With rescale = TRUE, the smoothing parameter is first divided by the penalty's scaling factor. These components describe the penalty on coefficients, rather than the variation in fitted term values over the observations.

Confidence intervals use the Hessian of the likelihood-based smoothness selection criterion, transformed to the log standard deviation scale. Shared smoothing parameters retain their shared uncertainty. A fixed smoothing parameter can still have an interval when the model scale is estimated. The scale is included as a separate row when its uncertainty is available. Unavailable intervals are NA.

For mgcv::gamm() fits, components are extracted from lme. Smooth variances are expressed on the same penalty scale as for gam() and bam(), with one row per penalty. Additional random effects have one row per coefficient variance, labelled by grouping factor and coefficient; their covariances are omitted. Intervals use nlme::intervals() when the fitted covariance parameters support this calculation. Bounds are NA when that information is unavailable, including fits containing pdTens tensor-product blocks. The estimated residual scale is labelled scale; a fixed scale is omitted. With residual variance weights, scale is the baseline variance before those weights are applied. For models fitted by penalized quasi-likelihood (PQL), these are approximate components of the working mixed model.

For gamm4::gamm4() fits, components are extracted from mer. Smooth components use the same penalty scale and labels as the other methods; additional random effects retain their mixed-model variances. By default, intervals are computed separately for each standard deviation using stats::profile() and stats::confint(). The profiling uses the fitted random-effects design matrices. Gaussian models are refitted by maximum likelihood for these profiles, including models fitted by REML; the reported point estimates remain those of the original fit. Profiling can take substantially longer than extracting estimates. Use interval_method = "none" for estimates without intervals. Failed profiles warn and return NA bounds for the affected component. Profiles are unavailable for generalized mixed models with an estimated scale.

With type = "terms", each component is a fitted term's contribution to the linear predictor, evaluated over the observations used to fit the model. Parametric formula terms are included, with all coefficients of a factor, polynomial or interaction combined into one term. Each smooth has one row, including smooths with several penalties. Additional random effects in gamm() and gamm4() contribute one component per grouping factor and coefficient, evaluated at their fitted values. Formula terms follow the model's contrast coding. Duplicated component labels receive numeric suffixes.

Term variances and covariances use equal observation weights and the sample denominator, the number of fitting observations minus one. Likelihood weights do not change this averaging. Intercepts, offsets and residual variation are excluded. rescale and interval_method apply only to type = "penalty"; no profiling is performed for term variances.

A final row labelled total gives the variance of the sum of the term contributions, including additional fitted random effects. It includes covariance between terms: the total is the sum of all entries of their covariance matrix, rather than just its diagonal. Models with several linear predictors have one total per predictor, labelled total, total.1, and so on in predictor order. A term shared by several predictors contributes to each of their totals. An intercept-only predictor has total variance zero. These labels are reserved; a formula term with the same name receives a numeric suffix so it remains distinct from the total. Use include_total = FALSE to omit the total rows and their columns in the posterior draw matrices. Totals are still calculated for proportions; the individual term estimates and intervals are unchanged.

Proportions allocate the total variance using $$p_j = \frac{\operatorname{Cov}(f_j, \sum_k f_k)} {\operatorname{Var}(\sum_k f_k)}.$$ Each term receives its own variance plus its covariance with the other terms. This splits each pair's covariance contribution equally between its two terms, so the individual proportions sum to one. Proportions can be negative or greater than one when terms offset each other's variation; they are not restricted to the interval from zero to one.

.proportion reports these allocations, with equal-tailed posterior bounds in .proportion_lower_ci and .proportion_upper_ci. These bounds are on the proportion scale. Each posterior proportion uses the term contributions and total from the same joint draw. Individual interval limits need not sum to one. The total row's proportion is one. For additional linear predictors, the columns receive suffixes .1, .2, and so on, matching the total labels; for example, .proportion.1 and .proportion_lower_ci.1. A shared term has a separate allocation for each predictor. Entries for unrelated terms and totals are NA.

Proportions are undefined when the total variance is zero and are returned as NA, including for an intercept-only predictor. Posterior draws with zero total variance retain NA proportions and are omitted when computing proportion intervals; if none are defined, both bounds are NA.

Term intervals are equal-tailed posterior intervals, computed by drawing the full coefficient vector from its approximate Gaussian posterior and recalculating each term's variance over the same fitting observations. All terms use the same coefficient draw in each replicate, preserving their dependence. Each total is calculated by summing the term contributions within that draw and then computing their variance. Additional fitted random effects in mixed models are drawn conditional on the GAM coefficients, retaining their covariance with the GAM terms and with each other. Smoothing parameters, random-effect covariance parameters and the response scale are held at their fitted values, unless unconditional = TRUE supplies a correction for smoothing-parameter uncertainty in the GAM coefficient covariance. PQL and generalized mixed models use the Gaussian approximation at the fitted working model. For SCAM fits, draws are made jointly on the unrestricted fitting scale and transformed before evaluating the terms.

Point estimates remain the variances of the fitted contributions. Interval bounds are quantiles of the posterior term standard deviations; square the bounds to obtain intervals for the term variances. Use seed for reproducible draws and n_draws = 0 to skip intervals and return NA bounds.

The covariance attribute contains the covariance matrix of the fitted term contributions, with rows and columns in .component order, excluding the total rows. Its diagonal equals .variance for the individual terms. For a model with a single linear predictor, the sum of all matrix entries equals the total row's .variance. Adding only the diagonal omits covariance between terms. This matrix describes variation across observations, rather than estimation uncertainty. When intervals are computed, the variance_draws attribute contains a matrix with one row per posterior draw and one column per component, on the variance scale. Rows are paired across terms. Its column names match .component; the coverage attribute records the requested interval coverage. The total columns include covariance between term contributions within each draw. Summing the individual term variances would omit that covariance. The proportion_draws attribute is a named list with one matrix per total (total, total.1, and so on). Each matrix has the same rows and columns as variance_draws, with NA entries for unrelated components. Its rows retain the pairing with the coefficient and variance draws. Proportions and their intervals are added only for type = "terms". The term_groups attribute lists the component labels belonging to each predictor, named by its total label. Use draw.variance_comp() to plot components or proportions with their stored intervals.
